verdict: Voting sharply reduces flakiness (N=5 flip-rate cut 34%) but cannot fix bias-driven errors; adaptive re-sampling did not meet the 90%-stability-at-<60%-cost target in this simulation.

outcomes.case: N=5 vote cuts flip rate by >70%
N=5 vote raises accuracy on borderline cases
Adaptive keeps >=90% of vote-5 stability gain at <60% of its calls
outcomes.evidence: stability ratio 0.99, call ratio 0.78 (3.91 vs 5.00 calls/case)
biased-tier acc 0.301 -> 0.155 (change -0.147); voting amplifies a wrong majority

chart.title: Flip rate vs judge calls per case

notes: The judge is a seeded deterministic STUB, not a real LLM; probabilities are assumptions.
Judge calls are assumed independent; real samples at temperature>0 share prompt-level bias and correlate, so real gains are likely smaller.
Tier mix and p_correct values are fixed up front and not tuned; conclusions depend on them.
Flip rate counts a case as flaky if any of 200 reruns disagrees, so it is sensitive to rerun count.
Adaptive escalates only when the first 3 votes disagree; confident-but-wrong verdicts are never re-checked.
